Text Inputs

Text fields, textareas, file inputs, and character counters.

Wrap the control and its label in .input-field. That wrapper is required for the floating label, supporting text, and prefix/suffix layout.

Add placeholder=" " (a single space) so the label can float with CSS only. A missing placeholder, or any other placeholder string, keeps the label in the floated position. Importing the bundle runs Forms.Init(); it validates .validate fields on change and starts textareas and file paths. Character Counter is not in AutoInit().

Supporting Text
place
gps_fixed
bubble_chart
error
Invalid characters! Please use 0-9 only. 
<form class="row">
  <div class="s12 m6 input-field">
    <input id="first_name" type="text" placeholder=" " maxlength="20">
    <label for="first_name">First Name</label>
    <span class="supporting-text">Supporting Text</span>
  </div>

  <div class="s12 m6 input-field outlined">
    <input id="last_name" type="text" placeholder=" " maxlength="20">
    <label for="last_name">Last Name</label>
  </div>

  <div class="s12 m6 input-field">
    <input id="disabled" type="text" placeholder=" " value="I am not editable" disabled>
    <label for="disabled">Disabled</label>
  </div>

  <div class="s12 m6 input-field">
    <div class="prefix"><i class="material-icons">place</i></div>
    <div class="suffix"><i class="material-icons">gps_fixed</i></div>
    <input id="inp-location" type="text" placeholder=" " value="Planet Earth">
    <label for="inp-location">Location</label>
  </div>

  <div class="s12 m6 input-field outlined">
    <div class="prefix"><i class="material-icons">bubble_chart</i></div>
    <div class="suffix"><i class="material-icons">error</i></div>
    <input id="inp-error" class="invalid" type="text" placeholder=" " value="$%/'#sdf">
    <label for="inp-error">Failing Input</label>
    <span class="supporting-text">Invalid characters! Please use 0-9 only.</span>
  </div>
</form>

The underline style is the default. Add outlined for a full border. Put invalid on the input for the error underline. Do not put error on the wrapper: that class is a color utility and fills the field with the error color. The helper line is .supporting-text, not .helper-text.

Input Types

email, password, and the other native text-like types are styled the same way. validate uses HTML5 constraint validation on change and toggles invalid on the input. There is no green valid style.

Supporting text for additional information 
<div class="s12 m6 input-field">
  <input id="email" type="email" class="validate" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <span class="supporting-text" data-error="wrong">
    Supporting text for additional information
  </span>
</div>
<div class="s12 m6 input-field">
  <input id="password" type="password" class="validate" placeholder=" " maxlength="20">
  <label for="password">Password</label>
</div>
Inline Inputs

Add inline to sit the field in a line of text.

This is an inline input field: 

This is an inline input field:
<span class="input-field inline">
  <input id="email_inline" type="email" class="validate" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="email_inline">Email</label>
</span>
Floating Labels

Labels float with CSS. Use placeholder=" " (one space). Any other placeholder string is treated as a real hint and the label stays floated. 

<div class="input-field outlined">
  <input id="first_name2" type="text" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="first_name2">First Name</label>
</div>
<div class="input-field outlined">
  <input id="last_name2" type="text" placeholder="Doe…">
  <label for="last_name2">Last Name</label>
</div>
Icon Prefixes

Put prefix on an icon, or wrap the icon in .prefix, before the input and label.

account_circle
phone 
<div class="input-field">
  <i class="material-icons prefix">account_circle</i>
  <input id="icon_prefix" type="text" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="icon_prefix">First Name</label>
</div>
Icon Suffixes

Same idea with suffix, still before the input in the markup.

account_circle
phone 
<div class="input-field">
  <i class="material-icons suffix">account_circle</i>
  <input id="icon_suffix" type="text" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="icon_suffix">First Name</label>
</div>
Custom Error Messages

Put data-error on .supporting-text. When the input has invalid, that string replaces the supporting text. There is no data-success style.

Helper text 
<div class="input-field">
  <input id="email" type="email" class="validate" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <span class="supporting-text" data-error="wrong">Helper text</span>
</div>

validate also honors a data-length attribute: the field is marked invalid when the value is longer than that number. Prefer maxlength when you want the browser to cap input; use data-length only if you want the validate check without a hard cap.

Changing colors

Focus, label, and underline color come from --input-color on .input-field, which defaults to --md-sys-color-primary. Override the token rather than restyling each state: 

.input-field {
  --input-color: var(--md-sys-color-tertiary);
}

Textarea

Use textarea.routeplate-textarea inside .input-field. That class name is RoutePlate’s; there is no .materialize-textarea. Textareas grow with their content. Forms.Init() starts every .routeplate-textarea on DOMContentLoaded. 

<div class="input-field">
  <textarea id="textarea1" class="routeplate-textarea" placeholder=" "></textarea>
  <label for="textarea1">Textarea</label>
</div>
<div class="input-field">
  <textarea id="textarea2" class="routeplate-textarea" placeholder="A custom placeholder :)"></textarea>
  <label for="textarea2">Textarea with placeholder</label>
</div>

If you add a textarea after load, initialize it yourself:

RoutePlate.Forms.InitTextarea(document.querySelector('#textarea1'));

Setting .value in script does not resize the field. Call textareaAutoResize afterwards: 

const el = document.querySelector('#textarea1');
el.value = 'New Text';
RoutePlate.Forms.textareaAutoResize(el);
Icon Prefixes
mode_edit 
<div class="input-field">
  <i class="material-icons prefix">mode_edit</i>
  <textarea id="icon_prefix2" class="routeplate-textarea" placeholder=" "></textarea>
  <label for="icon_prefix2">Message</label>
</div>

File Input

A .file-field.input-field pairs a button with a path field. Forms.Init() copies the chosen file name into input.file-path.

File 
<div class="file-field input-field">
  <div class="btn filled">
    <span>File</span>
    <input type="file">
  </div>
  <div class="file-path-wrapper">
    <input class="file-path" type="text" placeholder=" ">
  </div>
</div>

Add multiple to allow more than one file. The path field lists the names, comma-separated.

File 
<input type="file" multiple>

If you add a file input after load:

RoutePlate.Forms.InitFileInputPath(document.querySelector('#fileinput1'));

Character Counter

Character Counter is not in AutoInit(). It reads maxlength (not data-length) and writes current/max into a .character-counter span. Overflow adds invalid on the field. 

<div class="input-field">
  <input id="input_text" type="text" maxlength="10" placeholder=" ">
  <label for="input_text">Input text</label>
</div>
<div class="input-field">
  <textarea id="textarea2" class="routeplate-textarea" maxlength="120" placeholder=" "></textarea>
  <label for="textarea2">Textarea</label>
</div>
Initialization

There are no options. Initialize each field yourself, including ones added later.

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('#input_text, #textarea2');
  RoutePlate.CharacterCounter.init(elems);
});
